course.title: General Chemistry (lecture and laboratory)
course.instructor_identified_from: the archived lecture syllabus names the lecture instructor; the lab syllabus lists several section instructors, and which one taught this student's section is not recorded

coverage.notes: No lab report survives, and that is structural, not a filing gap. The archived lab syllabus says each report was written and handed in on paper before the end of the lab period, from a weekly lab manual posted online, which was not kept. It also says what the reports were graded on: correct calculations, units, significant figures, and reasonable answers to the questions, not the data itself. Lecture homework and daily quizzes were online. The in-class tests were handwritten on printed exams and are out of scope. The lecture syllabus describes an end-of-term sustainability essay, but its prompt was on Moodle and was not kept. One completed essay survives in a separate cloud folder, so the family is known but its length, citation, and format requirements are not. No format rule can be stated for anything in this course.

course_policy.summary: The archived syllabi cover collaboration, plagiarism, and cheating but contain no generative-AI statement. The current terms are unknown.
